messages.subject: Re: Stacked Bar Plot With Ordered Stacking
parts:
Well...after some additional digging I think I found the answer.

I needed to pass an ordering factor to the aes call. I ended up
creating a column that contained an ordered list of factors (in my
case I used numbers and then called them factors in the plotting call.
), tzone = "", class = c("POSIXct", "POSIXt")), spans =
structure(1305183600, class = c("POSIXct",
1305702000), tzone = "", class = c("POSIXct", "POSIXt")),

NewMachineState = c("Synth",
"Synth", "Synth", "Error", "Error", "Synth", "Error", "Error",
"Synth", "Synth", "Error", "Error", "Synth", "Synth", "Idle",
"Idle", "Synth", "Error", "Error", "Synth", "Error", "Error",
"Synth", "Error", "Error", "Synth", "Idle", "Idle", "Synth",
"Idle", "Idle", "Idle"), hours = c(24, 14.4630555555556,
0.763055555555556,
0.135277777777778, 0.128888888888889, 7.29666666666667,
0.152777777777778,
0.0983333333333333, 0.961944444444444, 2.15833333333333,
0.133888888888889,
0.125, 21.5827777777778, 1.12722222222222, 0.166666666666667,
0.390555555555556, 2.80111111111111, 0.615, 0.615277777777778,
0.691388888888889, 0.130277777777778, 0.685555555555556,
2.06833333333333,
0.220833333333333, 0.357222222222222, 1.54444444444444,
12.5861111111111,

15.1566666666667, 0.00333333333333333, 8.84, 24, 24), order = c(1L,
1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 4L,
5L, 6L, 7L, 8L, 9L, 10L, 11L, 12L, 13L, 14L, 1L, 2L, 3L, 1L,
1L)), .Names = c("TimeStamp", "spans", "lengths", "dayDate",
"NewMachineState", "hours", "order"), row.names = c(NA, 32L), class =
"data.frame")

plot = ggplot(df, aes( x = dayDate, y = hours, fill = NewMachineState,
order = as.factor( order ) ) )

plot + geom_bar(stat="identity",width=0.8,colour="black") +
scale_fill_manual(name="State",value=c("#FF7F00","#FFFF33","#4DAF4A"))
+ coord_flip()

That seems to give the timeline view that I was after.
